messages.author: 9d7d423218727f97
messages.subject: Generation of subtext in qplot
parts:
Is there an argument to qplot that is equivalent to the sub argument
to plot?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Generation of subtext in qplot
parts:
Hi:

I don't think there's a direct way to produce subtitles, but it's not hard to fake one:

qplot(1:10, 1:10) + xlab('x\n\nThis is a subtitle')

If you want different type sizes/fonts for each, that's a different problem...

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Generation of subtext in qplot
parts:
Hi:

On Thu, Dec 2, 2010 at 2:39 PM, Mark Sharp <msh...@sfbr.org> wrote:
Dennis,

Thank you for the assistance. I apologize for not being clear. I do need the smaller font for the subheading.
It is the cex.sub = 0.7 that goes with the sub argument that is critical in this situation.

The closest I can get is to use the grid.arrange() function from the gridExtra package, which does have a sub = argument, but uses conventions from the grid package with which I have, at best, cursory familiarity:

library(gridExtra)

grid.arrange(qplot(1:10, 1:10), sub = textGrob('This is a subtitle',
      vjust = 0.2, gp = gpar(cex = 0.7)))

See ?grid.arrange and ?textGrob for further details. I don't know if that's good enough for your purposes, but at least it's someplace to start.

Copied back to the group in case there are additional and/or better ideas.

HTH,
Dennis

Mark
R. Mark Sharp, Ph.D.
msh...@sfbr.org
